threads.thread_goal: Align on current routines, constraints, and select pilot group for the program.

messages.text: Hi team, welcome to the Integrated Wellbeing Program pilot. We have 21 days to design and launch a structured program that balances care, learning, and vocational skills for our youths. First step: we need to map what's already happening. Can everyone share observations on current weekly routines, school times, therapy appointments, and any informal activities the youths are already engaged in? This will help us identify realistic time windows for new activities. Please add notes to A1 (Current Youth Weekly Routines Overview) as you gather info. Also, let's start thinking about which youths might benefit most from this pilot—we want a mix of engagement levels and needs. Looking forward to your input.

Thanks for kicking this off. I've started documenting the routines for the past week. Most youths have school from 9 to 3, and we have therapy sessions scattered across afternoons. I noticed there's a gap between 4 and 5:30 pm on most days, and weekends are more flexible. I'll have the full week mapped by tomorrow. On the pilot group—I'd suggest including at least one youth who's been quieter lately, to see if structured activities help them engage more.

Good timing. I've reviewed the current schedule and I can see where vocational sessions could fit. The 4–5:30 pm window that 36599 mentioned looks solid for taster modules. I'd recommend we include youths with varying interests—some may lean toward practical skills, others toward creative work. I can help assess readiness once we have the full picture. Let me know what else you need from the vocational side.

I agree with including quieter youths. I'll add my observations to A1 as well. One thing I want to flag: we need to be careful about youths with recent trauma triggers. Some may find structured activities helpful, but we should check with the welfare officer before finalizing the group. I'll compile what I have by end of week.

Good point about trauma considerations. Let's make sure we have that conversation before we lock in the pilot group. 36599, can you and 4543 coordinate on the full routines map by EOD tomorrow? Once we have A1 complete, we can make a solid decision on D1—which youths are in the pilot. We also need to confirm D2: the exact time windows available. Let me know if you hit any blockers.

Will do. I'll have the full week of routines documented by tomorrow EOD. I'm also noting down the therapy and school times so we can see the real constraints. Should I also flag any youths who've expressed interest in specific activities? That might help with the co-design piece later.

Yes, absolutely. Youth interest is crucial for engagement. Once we have that, I can start sketching out which vocational modules might resonate. I'm thinking basic cooking, CV basics, and maybe workshop skills—but I want to see what the youths actually want to explore.
I can help with the routines mapping too. I've been tracking mood and incidents, so I can add context about which times are calmer or more challenging. Should I include that in A1 as well?

Yes, that's really helpful. Mood and incident patterns will help us schedule activities at times when youths are more receptive. Thanks for adding that layer. So to recap: 36599 and 4543 lead the routines map, 483681 adds mood/incident context, and 87396 starts thinking about vocational fit. We'll reconvene tomorrow to finalize A1 and make decisions on D1 and D2.

Sounds good. I'll coordinate with 36599 tomorrow morning to finalize the map. One more thing—should we also note any youths who might need extra support during transitions? That could affect how we structure the schedule.

Absolutely. That's exactly the kind of detail that will make the schedule work in practice. Add it to A1. Let's aim to have the full picture by tomorrow afternoon so we can confirm the pilot group and time windows by end of day.

Got it. I'll have the routines map ready by 3 pm tomorrow. I'll also note transition needs and any youths who've mentioned interest in specific activities. That should give us what we need to make the D1 and D2 calls.
Perfect. Once I see the routines and interest data, I can confirm which vocational modules fit the available slots. I'm confident we can make this work within the constraints.
Great. Let's reconvene tomorrow at 4 pm to review A1 and finalize D1 (pilot group) and D2 (time windows). I'll prepare a summary of the routines and we can make the calls together.

Sounds good. I'll have my notes ready. One last thing—should we also think about how we'll communicate the pilot to the youths? We want them to feel involved from the start, not like something's being done to them.

Excellent point. That's part of the co-design piece we'll tackle in the next thread. For now, let's lock in the group and time windows, then we'll move to activity design with youth input. See you all tomorrow at 4 pm.
Will do. I'll have everything ready by 3 pm so you have time to review before the call.
Thanks everyone. This is a solid start. Let's make sure A1 is complete and we're ready to decide on D1 and D2 tomorrow. Looking forward to moving forward with the schedule design next.

Update: A1 is now complete with full week routines, therapy/school times, mood patterns, and transition needs. Based on this data and team input, we're confirming D1 and D2. Pilot group: youths A, C, E, and G (mix of engagement levels, manageable for first cycle). Time windows confirmed: 4–5:30 pm weekdays for structured activities, flexible weekend slots. These decisions account for school hours, therapy appointments, and identified calm periods. Moving forward with schedule design in the next thread.
Great. The pilot group looks balanced. I'm confident these youths will engage well, and we have good time windows to work with. Ready to move to schedule design.
Confirmed. The 4–5:30 pm slot works perfectly for vocational modules. I can fit all three taster sessions into that window without conflicts. Ready to integrate into the full schedule.
Good decisions. The pilot group includes youths who will benefit from structure and those who need more engagement. Time windows are realistic. Let's move to the schedule design thread.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the weekly structured activity schedule and co-designed activities.

messages.text: Now that we have the pilot group and time windows locked in, let's design the weekly schedule. I've drafted a first version of A5 (Weekly Structured Activity and Vocational Schedule) that covers education support, leisure, and social skills blocks across the 4–5:30 pm window on weekdays. The schedule also reserves space for co-designed activities with youths. Please review A5 and give feedback on: (1) realistic fit with staff capacity, (2) balance of activity types, (3) where youth co-design should happen. Also, 36599, can you start gathering youth ideas for at least two activities they'd like to do? That's T6. Let me know your thoughts.

I've reviewed A5. The structure looks good, but I'm wondering about staff coverage. Do we have enough people to run education support and leisure activities at the same time? Also, I'll start the youth co-design conversations this week. I'm thinking a group discussion on Friday to gather ideas. Should I ask them what they'd like to learn or what they'd like to do for fun, or both?

On staff coverage: I can lead the vocational sessions, which frees up one person for education support. That should help. On the youth co-design—ask for both. Some youths will want to learn practical skills, others want creative or social activities. The mix will help us design something that appeals to everyone.

Good question on staffing. Looking at A5, I think we can manage if we rotate: one person leads education support, another leads leisure/social, and 87396 handles vocational. That's three people for the 4–5:30 slot. We have that capacity most days. On youth co-design, I'd suggest asking open-ended questions—'What would make this time fun for you?' rather than leading them toward specific activities.

Good staffing plan. Let's confirm that works for everyone. 36599, go ahead with the Friday group discussion using open-ended questions. Document the ideas and we'll integrate the top two into A5 as part of D4. I want to make sure the youths see their input reflected in the final schedule.
Will do. I'll run the group discussion Friday and have the ideas documented by Monday. Then we can decide which two activities to include in the schedule.

I've looked at A5 and the structure makes sense. One thing I'd add: can we build in a short check-in at the start of each session? Just a few minutes to see how youths are feeling. That might help us catch any issues early and adjust activities if needed.
Great idea. I'll add a 5-minute check-in to the start of each session in A5. That aligns with our trauma-informed approach and gives us real-time feedback. Thanks for that.

The check-in is smart. It also gives me a sense of where youths are before I start a vocational session. I can adjust the pace or content if needed. I'm ready to finalize the schedule once we have the youth co-design ideas.

Agreed. The check-in will help with consistency across shifts too. Once 36599 has the youth ideas, we can lock in D3 (approve the schedule) and D4 (select co-designed activities). Should be ready by mid-week.

Yes, let's aim for mid-week approval. 36599, once you have the youth ideas, share them here and we'll make the D4 decision. Then I'll finalize A5 with the check-in and co-designed activities, and we'll confirm D3. Sound good?
Perfect. I'll have the youth ideas by Monday and we can decide on the two activities to include. Then the schedule will be ready for approval.
Great. Let's reconvene Monday afternoon to review the youth ideas and finalize D3 and D4. I'll have an updated A5 ready for approval by end of day Monday.
Sounds good. I'll be ready to review and approve on Monday.
Ready. Once the schedule is approved, I can finalize the vocational module details and timing.

Youth co-design ideas from Friday discussion: youths want to do cooking together (practical and social), art/creative time, and a weekly game night. Top two choices: cooking and game night. Both are feasible and align with the schedule. Ready to integrate into A5.

Excellent. Cooking and game night are perfect—practical, social, and fun. D4 confirmed: we'll include these two co-designed activities in the schedule. I'm updating A5 now with the check-in, cooking session on Wednesdays, and game night on Fridays. Should have the final version ready by EOD today.
Great choices. The youths will feel heard, which is exactly what we want. Ready to review the final A5.
Perfect. Cooking and game night fit well with the vocational and social skills goals. I can work around those activities with the taster modules.

Final A5 is now uploaded. It includes the 5-minute check-in at the start of each session, education support blocks, leisure/social skills, vocational taster slots, and the two co-designed activities (cooking Wednesday, game night Friday). D3 confirmed: the weekly structured activity schedule is approved and ready for pilot launch. Next thread will cover the tools and templates.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on templates and tools: individual plans, handover checklist, and monitoring log.

messages.text: Now that the schedule is locked in, let's finalize the tools we'll use to track and support each youth. I've drafted three key templates: A2 (Individual Support and Development Plan Template), A4 (Shift Handover and Coordination Checklist), and A7 (Wellbeing and Engagement Monitoring Log). These are designed to be simple enough for all shifts to use consistently. Please review each and give feedback on: (1) clarity and usability, (2) whether sections are complete, (3) any missing elements. Let me know your thoughts by EOD tomorrow so we can finalize D5 and D6.

I've reviewed A2 and A4. A2 looks comprehensive—it covers wellbeing, social skills, education, and risk indicators. I'd suggest adding a section for 'youth strengths' so we're not just documenting needs. On A4, the checklist is clear, but I'm wondering if we should add a line for 'mood at handover' so the next shift knows how the youth is feeling right now.

Good suggestions. I agree on the strengths section in A2—that's important for a positive approach. On A4, the mood line is essential. We also need a line for 'any incidents or concerns' so nothing gets missed between shifts. I'll review A7 and get back to you.

I've looked at all three. A2 is solid, and I like the strengths addition. For A4, the mood and incidents lines are crucial. On A7, the monitoring log looks good, but I'd suggest we keep the indicators simple—maybe just participation, mood, and any conflicts. Too many metrics will overwhelm staff.

I agree on keeping A7 simple. I've been tracking mood and participation informally, and those two plus incidents cover what we really need to know. Adding too much will make it hard to sustain. A2 and A4 look good with the suggested additions.

Great feedback. I'm updating all three templates: A2 will include a 'youth strengths' section, A4 will add 'mood at handover' and 'incidents/concerns' lines, and A7 will focus on three indicators: participation, mood, and conflicts. This keeps things manageable. I'll have the revised versions ready by EOD today. Can everyone review and confirm by tomorrow morning so we can lock in D5 and D6?
Will do. I'll review the updated versions first thing tomorrow and confirm they work for us.
Ready to review tomorrow. I think these updates will make the tools much more practical for daily use.
I'll review tomorrow. The simplified A7 will definitely help with consistency across shifts.
I'll review first thing tomorrow. These changes sound good.

Updated templates are now live: A2 includes youth strengths section, A4 has mood and incidents lines, A7 focuses on three simple indicators. All templates have been reviewed and approved by the team. D5 confirmed: Individual Support and Development Plan template is approved for use. D6 confirmed: Shift handover checklist and monitoring indicators are finalized. These tools are ready for staff training and pilot launch.
Great. The templates are clear and practical. Ready to move forward with staff training.
Confirmed. These tools will make handovers much smoother and ensure we're tracking what matters.
Good to go. The simplified monitoring will help us stay focused on what's important.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and coordinate vocational skills taster modules within the weekly schedule.

messages.text: I've finalized the vocational skills taster module plan (A6). I'm proposing three modules for the first pilot cycle: (1) Basic Cooking—practical life skills, food safety, teamwork; (2) CV Basics—understanding strengths, writing a simple CV, job search intro; (3) Workshop Skills—tool safety, basic woodworking or craft. Each module is 4 weeks, one session per week, 45 minutes. I'm proposing: Cooking on Mondays, CV Basics on Tuesdays, Workshop Skills on Thursdays, all in the 4–5:30 pm slot. This avoids conflicts with school and therapy. Please review A6 and confirm: (1) module content is appropriate, (2) timing works, (3) group size is manageable. Let me know if you'd like adjustments.

I've reviewed A6. The modules look great and the timing fits perfectly with the schedule. The youths will be excited about cooking and CV basics especially. Workshop skills might need some prep on tool safety, but that's doable. Group size of 4 youths per session is manageable. I'd suggest we start with cooking and CV basics, then add workshop skills in week 3 if the first two go well.

I agree. The modules are well-designed. I'd add one thing: can we build in a reflection piece at the end of each session? Just a few minutes for youths to say what they learned or what they'd like to try next. That keeps them engaged and gives us feedback.
Good idea. I'll add a 5-minute reflection at the end of each session. That aligns with our feedback approach and helps youths think about what they're learning. I'll update A6 to include that.
The modules sound good. I like the phased approach—start with two, add the third if it's working. That's smart risk management. The reflection piece is also good for tracking engagement.

Excellent feedback. 87396, can you confirm the final timing for D8? I want to make sure the vocational sessions don't clash with anything else. Also, let's confirm D7: which modules are we running in the first cycle?

D7: We're starting with Cooking and CV Basics, adding Workshop Skills in week 3 if all goes well. D8: Cooking on Mondays 4–4:45 pm, CV Basics on Tuesdays 4–4:45 pm, Workshop Skills on Thursdays 4–4:45 pm (starting week 3). All times are clear of school and therapy. I've checked against A1 and A5—no conflicts.
Perfect. The timing is solid and the phased approach gives us flexibility. I'm ready to support the sessions and help with setup.
Confirmed. The timing works and the phased rollout is smart. I'll be ready to support and help with the reflection piece.

D7 and D8 confirmed. Cooking and CV Basics start immediately, Workshop Skills in week 3. All times locked in and conflict-free. 87396, can you finalize A6 with the reflection piece and any other details, and we'll be ready for staff training?
Will do. I'll finalize A6 with the reflection piece and have it ready by EOD today. I'll also prepare brief talking points for staff training on the vocational approach.

Great. Once A6 is finalized, we'll include it in the staff training materials. The vocational modules are a key part of the program, so clear talking points will help everyone understand the goals and approach.
Ready for training. I'll make sure the youths know what to expect and get them excited about the modules.

A6 is finalized with all module details, timing, materials, and the 5-minute reflection piece. Vocational modules are ready for pilot launch. D7 confirmed: Cooking and CV Basics start immediately, Workshop Skills in week 3. D8 confirmed: Cooking Mondays 4–4:45 pm, CV Basics Tuesdays 4–4:45 pm, Workshop Skills Thursdays 4–4:45 pm (week 3+). All times conflict-free with school and therapy.
Excellent. The vocational plan is solid and well-timed. Ready to launch.
Great. The youths will benefit from these modules. Ready to support.

threads.thread_goal: Review first two weeks of pilot, discuss incidents, and agree on adjustments.

messages.text: We're two weeks into the pilot. Time to review what's working and what needs adjustment. I've compiled feedback from youths, staff observations, and monitoring data into A8 (Pilot Feedback Summary Note). Key themes: (1) youths are engaged in cooking and game night, (2) CV basics needs more interactive elements, (3) one youth (E) is struggling with group settings, (4) handover checklist is working well, (5) monitoring log is simple and sustainable. I'm proposing adjustments: make CV basics more hands-on, consider one-on-one support for youth E, keep cooking and game night as is. Please review A8 and share your observations. We need to decide on D1 (reconfirm pilot group) and D4 (adjust co-designed activities) based on what we're learning.

I've reviewed A8. The feedback aligns with what I'm seeing. Cooking is definitely a hit—youths are engaged and learning. Game night is fun and builds social skills. CV basics needs work; youths found it too lecture-y. On youth E: I've noticed they're quieter in group settings but engaged one-on-one. I'd suggest we keep them in the pilot but offer some individual check-ins alongside the group activities. That might help them feel more comfortable.

I agree on youth E. Keeping them in with individual support is the right call. On CV basics, I'd suggest making it more interactive—maybe have youths interview each other about their strengths, then write a simple CV together. That's more engaging than a presentation. Also, I've noticed the handover checklist is working really well; staff are using it consistently.

Good observations. On CV basics, the peer interview idea is solid. I can incorporate that into the next session. On youth E, individual support alongside group activities is a good balance. I've also noticed that the cooking module is building confidence—youths are trying new things and supporting each other. That's exactly what we want.

I've been tracking mood and participation in A7. Cooking and game night show consistent high engagement. CV basics shows lower engagement. Youth E's mood is stable but participation is lower in group settings. The monitoring data supports the feedback. I'd also note that the check-in at the start of sessions is helping us catch issues early.

Thanks for the data. It's clear that cooking and game night are working well, and we need to adjust CV basics. On youth E, the individual support approach makes sense. Let me propose the adjustments for D1 and D4: D1—keep the pilot group as is (youths A, C, E, G) but add individual check-ins for youth E. D4—keep cooking and game night, replace or redesign CV basics to be more interactive (peer interviews). Does that align with what everyone's seeing?

Yes, that aligns. Keeping the group and adding support for youth E is the right call. And redesigning CV basics with peer interviews will make it more engaging. I can help facilitate those conversations.
Agreed. The adjustments make sense. Youth E will benefit from the individual support, and the peer interview approach will make CV basics more meaningful.

I'm on board. The peer interview approach is more aligned with our pedagogy anyway. I'll redesign the CV basics session for next week with that structure. Youth E's individual support will help them feel more included.
The adjustments are sound. Individual support for youth E and the redesigned CV basics should improve engagement. I'll continue tracking in A7 to see the impact.

Great. D1 and D4 are confirmed. I'm updating A8 with the agreed adjustments and will document the changes in A5 (schedule) and A6 (vocational modules). 36599, can you start the individual check-ins with youth E this week? 87396, can you redesign the CV basics session with peer interviews for next week? I'll update the documentation by EOD today.
Will do. I'll start individual check-ins with youth E this week. Just a few minutes to see how they're doing and what they need. Should help them feel more supported.
I'll redesign CV basics with the peer interview structure and have it ready for next week. That should make it much more engaging.
Perfect. Let's reconvene in one week to review the impact of these adjustments. I'll also prepare a brief update for the team on what we're learning from the pilot so far.
Good plan. The adjustments should help. I'll keep an eye on youth E and the CV basics sessions and report back.
I'll continue monitoring and will have updated data by next week. Looking forward to seeing the impact of the adjustments.

Pilot review complete. Key adjustments implemented: (1) Individual check-ins added for youth E to support group participation. (2) CV basics redesigned with peer interviews for better engagement. (3) Cooking and game night continue as planned—both showing strong engagement. (4) Monitoring data shows positive trends in participation and mood for youths A, C, and G. D1 reconfirmed: pilot group remains youths A, C, E, G with enhanced support for E. D4 reconfirmed: cooking and game night continue, CV basics redesigned. Updated documentation in A5, A6, and A8. Pilot is on track for successful completion.
Excellent summary. The adjustments are already showing positive results. Youth E is more engaged with the individual check-ins, and the peer interview approach for CV basics is much better received.
The adjustments are working well. The peer interview structure for CV basics is more engaging, and youths are learning from each other. Cooking continues to be a highlight.
Great progress. The pilot is delivering on its goals. Looking forward to the final weeks and the retrospective.
